skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

2.

8.

10.    - **Deleted** `global size_of usize == 8;` (and its comment) at the top of the file —
11.      this was the source of the `error[E0080]: ... does not have the expected size`
12.      codegen panic on the default `TARGET=x86` build.
13.    - **Strengthened `Inner::internal_inv`** with the correct representability conjunct:
14.      ```rust
15.      // Every managed bitmap index is a representable frame number. Established by `init`,
16.      // which sizes the bitmap from `MEMORY_SIZE / FRAME_SIZE` (far below
17.      // `FrameNumber::spec_max()`), so `from_raw_value`/`from_frame_number` never reject an
18.      // in-range index. Target-agnostic; holds on both 32- and 64-bit builds.
19.      &&& self.bitmap@.num_bits <= FrameNumber::spec_max() + 1
20.      ```
21.      This is the real fact established by the allow-listed TCB boundary (`init`/`instance`,
22.      which `ensures (*r).inv()`), so it is sound to assume from the trust boundary. It is
23.      preserved by every proof target because `num_bits` is never resized.
24. 
25. 2. **`src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs`**
26.    - **`Inner::alloc`** (was lines ~155–181): removed the now-unused exec binding
27.      `let nbits = self.bitmap.number_of_bits();` and the word-size reasoning
28.      (`nbits < u32::MAX`, `(u32::MAX as int) <= spec_max() by (compute)`). The conversion
29.      bound is now discharged directly from the invariant:
30.      ```rust
31.      assert(idx < self.bitmap@.num_bits);
32.      assert(self.bitmap@.num_bits <= FrameNumber::spec_max() + 1);
33.      assert(idx <= FrameNumber::spec_max());
34.      ```
35.    - **`Inner::alloc_contiguous`** (was lines ~340–347): replaced
36.      `assert((u32::MAX as int) <= FrameNumber::spec_max()) by (compute);` with
37.      `assert(self.bitmap@.num_bits <= FrameNumber::spec_max() + 1);` so the
38.      `from_raw_value` `None`-branch is discharged from the invariant rather than the word
39.      size.
40. 
41. 3. **`verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-frame/bugs.md`**
42.    - Marked both the "top-of-memory frame unrepresentable" bug and the
43.      "`global size_of usize == 8` directive" entries as **RESOLVED**, documenting the
44.      invariant-based fix (this is a record update reflecting the actual code change, not a
45.      justification to close the item).
46. 
47. No locked top-level spec (`Inner::share/refcount/is_covered/free/book/alloc_range/
48. alloc_contiguous/alloc`) was weakened. The change to `internal_inv` is a **strengthening**
49. (adds a guarantee), not a weakening, and is the change the reviewer explicitly required.
50. No `external_body` was added.
51. 
52. ### Verification
53. 
54. **`make verify-kernel` (default `TARGET=x86`):**
55. ```
56. verification: 112 verified, 0 errors (exit 0)
57. ```
58. No `error[E0080]`. The const-eval codegen panic is gone — the command now compiles to
59. exit 0.
60. 
61. **`make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys` (default `TARGET=x86`):**
62. ```
63. verification: 82 verified, 0 errors (exit 0)
64. ```
65. (`status: CHEATING_DETECTED` reflects only out-of-scope `admit`s in `manager.proof.rs` /
66. `mod.proof.rs` and the allow-listed `external_body` wrappers; frame scope has
67. `admit=0, assume=0`.)
68. 
69. **`./z build` (default `TARGET=x86`, non-`verus_keep_ghost` codegen):**
70. ```
71. [OK]    Build complete.
72. EXIT=0
73. ```
74. (There is no `make build` target in the Makefile; `./z build` is the repository's build
75. command. It exercises the real non-ghost codegen path, which is where the E0080 would
76. surface — it does not.)
77. 
78. **`make verify` (all verified crates, default `TARGET=x86`):** all crates exit 0, 0 errors.
79. 
80. **Cross-target `make verify-kernel TARGET=x86_64`:** the frame proofs no longer depend on
81. word size, but the **whole-kernel x86_64 build does not compile for a pre-existing,
82. unrelated reason** in an arch module I did not touch:

84. error[E0433]: cannot find `Idt` in `idt`
85.  (src/kernel/src/hal/arch/x86_64/cpu/idt.rs)
86. error: could not compile `kernel` (bin "kernel") due to 1 previous error

90. it is independent of `mm::phys::frame` (my diff is confined to `frame.rs` /
91. `frame.proof.rs` / `bugs.md`). The fix itself is target-agnostic: the representability
92. bound is now `num_bits <= spec_max() + 1` for whatever `spec_max()` the target defines, so
93. it no longer assumes `usize == 8`.
94. 
95. ### Result: FIXED

98. representability bound is carried by the (strengthened) `internal_inv`, and on the default

105. `arch/x86_64/cpu/idt.rs` compile error outside this module's scope; it prevents Verus from
106. running at all and is not caused by, nor fixable within, the frame allocator.
